subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Shoply) - follow-up
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@shoply.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Shoply) - follow-up

Alex — thanks again for the conversation today. Below is a concise recap of pain points, current stack, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we can move to a technical deep dive next week. Reply with any corrections or additions.

Pain points
- Rising per-token costs from current OpenAI usage across chat and embeddings, especially during campaign spikes.
- Throttling/rate-limit impacts during promotions — leads to degraded UX and increased retries.
- Compliance: need VPC controls, detailed audit logs, and KMS integration for customer data.

Current stack (what we discussed)
- OpenAI: gpt-4o-mini for chat; text-embedding-3-large (1536 dims) for semantic search.
- Anthropic: used for a limited set of safety-sensitive workflows (account recovery).
- Orchestration: custom gateway with feature flags; nightly batch reindex jobs for embeddings.
- Volume profile: ~800k tokens/day baseline, up to ~2.5M tokens/day during peaks.

Success criteria for migration
1) Cost reduction: target ~35%+ per-unit cost savings while preserving latency SLOs.
2) Compatibility: minimal SDK/contract changes — chat+streaming and embeddings endpoints.
3) Quality: maintain or improve NLU for recommendations and search.
4) Ops: VPC/private deployment option, KMS support, SSO, and audit logs.

Compatibility considerations
- Streaming/chat API parity and stable API surface for minimal code changes.
- Embeddings: need plan for dimension mismatch and staged reindexing of ~20M records.
- Tokenization differences: guidance and recommended prompt templates to reduce regressions.
- Auth: API keys plus enterprise credential integration (KMS/HSM).

Model shortlist (initial candidates)
- Llama 2 / Meta variants — strong chat, licensing to review.
- Mistral-instruct family — competitive instruction following and cost profile.
- RedPajama / Falcon derivatives — solid base for both embeddings and chat with quant options.
- Lightweight embedding-only models for batch reindex workloads to reduce cost.

Proposed next steps
- Rishi/Marissa: send technical requirements stub + SOW template (attached).
- Alex: share a small, non-sensitive sample of prompt/response pairs and current embedding vector stats (dims, index size) by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule: technical deep dive (30–45m) with infra + inference engineers next week — Marissa to propose windows.

Attachments referenced: shoply-technical-requirements.pdf (stub), sow-template.docx.

If that aligns, we’ll prepare a short tech note on embedding-dimension migration strategies for the deep dive.

— Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

I’ll place a trimmed, PII-scrubbed sample of prompts and an embedding stats export in a shared Drive link by EOD tomorrow. Also attaching our internal latency targets (p95 < 300ms for chat).

One ask before the deep dive: can you include recommended approaches for handling embedding-dimensional mismatch (keep dual-index vs. reindex)?
